remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation already reflects current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows the enterprise refund-workflow weakness is actually disclosed in the current model card or certification packet.
No approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or owner sign-off is in evidence for the material segment weakness.
The certification position still depends on a future documentation update, which does not satisfy present compliance on this record.
The six-week-old approval and informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and cannot close the current policy predicate.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor narrowed the claim to a caveated position and made useful concessions, but provided no new admissible evidence. That is a reframing of the same record, not proof that the required policy condition is already satisfied. The policy text is explicit: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the evidence available to this role, those predicates remain unproven. This is not 'compliant_with_caveats' because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance requirement, not a bounded residual risk on top of demonstrated compliance. The overall readiness case may be plausible, but present compliance is still unsupported on the current record.
